circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has been the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne that hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year, alongside the local Supercars Championship event and various supporting race categories. The venue holds the highest FIA safety classification for motorsport circuits.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km Austrian motorsport venue situated in Spielberg, Styria, that has hosted the country's Formula One grand prix across two separate periods. Originally known as Österreichring, the circuit held the Austrian Grand Prix continuously from 1970 to 1987 before undergoing reconstruction and renaming as the A1-Ring, during which it again staged the race from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is a street track situated along Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan's capital, measuring 6. 003 km per lap and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One race in the Middle East that same year and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the FIA Grade 1 licensed facility accommodates various motorsport events including GP2 Series competition, endurance racing, and formerly hosted Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 to 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located near Barcelona in northeastern Spain, is a 4. 657-kilometer facility renowned for its balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand infrastructure.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been hosting Formula One racing since the inaugural 1950 season. The venue has staged the Belgian Grand Prix annually from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006, making it one of the championship's most enduring racing venues.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary road course that serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its primary role hosting the top tier of motorsport, the facility has accommodated numerous other racing series including sportscar championships and various North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility served as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 through 2019, resuming in 2024 after a hiatus. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix, which began in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: The Silverstone Circuit, located in the English Midlands near Northamptonshire, has served as the primary venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and was the inaugural race of the Formula One World Championship in 1950. After rotating with two other British circuits throughout the 1950s to 1980s, Silverstone became the permanent home of the British Grand Prix from 1987 onwards and continues to host major motorsport events including MotoGP.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the first Formula One venue to host a Grand Prix behind the Iron Curtain when it opened in 1986, after Bernie Ecclestone sought a race in Eastern Europe. Built in just eight months near a major highway outside the city, the 4. 381 km circuit was constructed faster than any other Formula One track and held its inaugural race on 24 March 1986 as a tribute to Hungarian motorcycle racing pioneer János Drapál.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 that ranks among the world's earliest purpose-built racing facilities and remains Europe's oldest on the mainland. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 (with only a 1980 interruption for renovation), it holds the distinction of being one of just four circuits to appear continuously on the Formula One calendar from the championship's inception, earning its nickname "the Temple of Speed" from its characteristic long straights and rapid-direction changes.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture and managed by Honda Mobilityland. The track, which accommodates 155,000 spectators, serves as a prominent host for both Formula One and Japanese Super Formula racing competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, following roads adjacent to downtown Las Vegas. The track incorporates iconic casino and hotel venues along Las Vegas Boulevard, weaving past recognizable landmarks such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two pioneering Mexican drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The track has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix during three distinct eras, with the current iteration beginning in 2015 and now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary 3. 363-mile circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design, the track was built specifically for the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of the Principality of Monaco, circling the harbour area. The circuit is frequently known as "Monte Carlo," reflecting that much of its layout occupies streets within the Monte Carlo neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining Formula One in 2021. The venue's involvement with the sport concluded following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419-kilometer racing venue featuring a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holding an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, a 4. 309 km circuit in São Paulo, opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years prior. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features supporting facilities including a karting venue dedicated to another notable Brazilian racing driver.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah. It has served as the host location for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually from 2021 onwards, and recently began hosting international electric racing competition.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront area, incorporating sections of the city's Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its urban racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya measures 4. 657 kilometers and features a versatile layout combining extended straightaways with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing various racing capabilities. The facility holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas spans 3. 426 miles and meets FIA Grade 1 standards for international motorsport competition. The venue currently hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside MotoGP and endurance racing events, having previously accommodated various other major racing series including IndyCar and sports car championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who currently represents Thailand in Formula One while driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships during his 23-season career with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship, two Le Mans 24 Hours titles, and the 2019 Daytona 24 Hours, making him the sole driver to secure both F1 and world sportscar championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Antonelli is an Italian driver who joined Mercedes' Formula One roster starting in 2025 and has secured eight Grand Prix victories during his early career in the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: British driver Oliver Bearman currently races for Haas in Formula One, competing at the sport's highest level.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races for Audi in Formula One, competing at the highest level of motorsport with the German manufacturer.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish driver, currently races in Formula One for Cadillac. Over his 13-season career, he has claimed 10 Grand Prix victories and twice finished as championship runner-up during his time with Mercedes, achieving these second-place finishes in 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver competing in Formula One with Alpine, bringing his racing talents to one of the sport's established teams.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas while pursuing his primary racing interests in European endurance competition with Nielsen Racing. He has made limited Formula One appearances, contesting seven Grands Prix during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French racing driver Pierre Gasly currently competes in Formula One for Alpine. He achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a French-Algerian motorsport competitor who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France in the championship.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding a record-tying seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including victories, pole positions, and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg is a German Formula One driver currently racing for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved success in endurance motorsport by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor who currently drives for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver currently competing for Ferrari, finished as championship runner-up in 2022 and has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver known as K-Mag, raced in Formula One across two separate periods between 2014 and 2024. He currently competes in the World Endurance Championship as a factory BMW driver for WRT, while also taking on part-time NASCAR duties with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: British driver Lando Norris secured the 2025 Formula One world championship while racing for McLaren, adding to his tally of 13 Grand Prix victories accumulated over his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French racing driver Esteban Ocon currently competes in Formula One for Haas. Earlier in his career, he achieved a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian round while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac after spending 15 seasons in the sport. He achieved his best championship result in 2023 when he finished as runner-up while driving for Red Bull, and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Vázquez de Castro currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12 seasons competing at the sport's highest level.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following previous stints in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently competing in Formula One, where he races for the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese motorsport competitor currently functioning as a reserve driver for both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. He participated as a full-time driver across the 2021-2025 seasons before transitioning to a reserve role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch and Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Max Verstappen has secured four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, the sole Chinese competitor to date in Formula One, raced in the championship during 2022-2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, operating as Renault's factory entry in the championship. Originally established under the Renault F1 Team name and backed by the French automotive conglomerate, the squad was rebranded to spotlight Renault's Alpine sports car marque before the manufacturer's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has entered Formula One racing through multiple incarnations as a British manufacturer, with its current competition operated under the AMR GP Limited entity and branded as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, participating continuously in the championship since its inception in 1950. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their distinctive emblem, Ferrari remains the sport's most decorated outfit throughout its seven-decade history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: The American-licensed outfit was founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014 and entered Formula One competition in 2016. Led by team principal Ayao Komatsu, who took over from long-time leader Guenther Steiner in early 2024, the squad continues to operate as a competitive midfield presence in the championship.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss racing enterprise established in 1970, this constructor competed in Formula One from 1993 onwards while building significant success in endurance motorsport, including a Le Mans victory in 1989. The team underwent various ownership transitions throughout its three-decade Formula One tenure before being acquired by Audi in 2024, eventually ceasing independent operations in 2025 as one of the championship's longest-serving independent constructors.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British racing outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking that competes in Formula One under corporate sponsorship. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group, with ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes-Benz has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and power unit supplier, with its current incarnation operating from Brackley under a German racing licence. The Mercedes-AMG Petronas team underwent a significant ownership restructuring in January 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff. The marque's racing heritage is epitomised by the enduring "Silver Arrows" moniker applied to its competitive entries.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that joined the grid in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the team operates as the junior outfit within the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the championship in 2024 as Red Bull GmbH's second team. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes alongside its sister team Red Bull Racing, the outfit represents the energy drink conglomerate's dual-team strategy in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England but racing under an Austrian licence, has been a dominant force in Formula One since its establishment in 2005 under long-time team principal Christian Horner, who led the squad until 2025. The team forms part of Red Bull GmbH's motorsport portfolio alongside the Racing Bulls outfit, and was succeeded in leadership by Laurent Mekies following Horner's departure.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of an earlier venture, Williams is a British Formula One constructor headquartered in Grove, Oxfordshire. The team operates as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in the 2026 season.
